item.title: Every player from California to play for the Golden State Warriors - John Coughran
item.description: The Golden State Warriors have signed, drafted, and traded for players from nearly every U.S. state and many countries around the world. From Alaska to Wyoming and Austria to Zaire, the Warriors have a strong history of seeking out talent necessary for NBA success. Since their beginnings in the Basketball Association of America (a precursor to the NBA) when they got their start as the team representing Philadelphia before they made their move to the West Coast, the organization has consistently pursued talent from a broad range of sources. For this installment of our series taking stock of the birthplace of every Golden State player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for the Warriors. Our focus in this article is John Coughran. An alum of Cal, he was picked up with the 74th overall selection of the 1973 NBA Draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers. The Pittsburg, California native played abroad the first 6 seasons of his pro career instead, signing with the Dubs in 1979. His stay with the team lasted until he was cut in 1980. During his time suiting up for the Warriors, Coughran put up 2.8 points per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. item.title: Former NFL QB reveals interest in Troy Aikman's 'Monday Night Football' gig at ESPN
item.description: Drew Brees (left) and Troy Aikman. Photos from The Associated Press and The Dallas Morning News. (SportsDay Staff) ESPN could have an intriguing candidate available if Troy Aikman decides to move on from his "Monday Night Football" analyst gig. In a recent interview with Front Office Sports , Drew Brees said he would be interested in the ESPN analyst role if Troy Aikman steps away. Brees wouldn't exactly be new to the gig, as he currently serves as an analyst for Fox Sports' NFL coverage. Last month, Aikman confirmed he would become a free agent after the 2026 NFL season concludes. When Front Office Sports' Baker Machado asked Brees if he would be interested in the ESPN job, the former New Orleans Saints quarterback offered a simple response. "Of course," Brees said. Fox Sports officially hired Brees as an NFL analyst in 2025. He shares the booth with play-by-play announcer Adam Amin as part of Fox's weekly NFL coverage. Brees was recently on the call for the Dallas Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts last week. “At the end of the day, I aspire to be the best at what I’m pursuing. I love broadcasting and I love my team. And I love being able to broadcast games every week,” Brees told Front Office Sports . “For example, this week, we’re broadcasting Vikings-Packers. The Packers are one of the most explosive offenses in football right now. I love the fact that I’ll get a chance to dive into watching [Packers QB] Jordan Love, [coach] Matt LaFleur and that whole offense. Look, they struggled early on in the season. Now they’ve kind of turned the corner. The Vikings are reeling a little bit. Trying to figure it out on offense. We get to dive in and identify what the solutions could be. The [Vikings] defense is lights out. What a great matchup that’s going to be. I get to be in the shoes of both.” In October, Front Office Sports reported that there was tension between Aikman and Joe Buck as they awaited new contracts at ESPN . Buck reached a new six-year deal with the network, but Aikman's wait is ongoing . "I don't know that it's hard to figure out kind of what's happened, but you know, I'll broadcast through this season and I'll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens," Aikman said. "But I'm looking forward to whatever the rest of this year does hold and with the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot might be." item.title: Ohio State adds another starting OL to availability report vs Northwestern
item.description: Ohio State football may have to play without two of its starting offensive linemen Nov. 14 against Northwestern. Buckeyes right tackle Phillip Daniels is listed as questionable on the availability report after missing four games earlier this season due to a lower-body injury he suffered against Texas on Sept. 12. Daniels returned to the starting lineup for all but one of the last three games. Left guard Luke Montgomery , meanwhile was downgraded from questionable to doubtful. Montgomery has started 27 consecutive games for Ohio State, dating back to the 2024 College Football Playoffs. The Buckeyes' offensive line has dealt with multiple issues throughout the season, which has repeatedly shuffled players' positions up front. Freshman wide receiver Brock Boyd , who has missed the last three games, was also moved from questionable to doubtful. The availability reports are released daily by the Big Ten, starting three days before each conference game is played, and the injuries are unspecified. Wide receivers Philip Bell and Brandon Inniss are expected to be available against Northwestern, as Bell was upgraded from questionable to probable and Inniss was taken off the availability report on Nov. 12. Ohio State has six players already ruled out, including quarterback Julian Sayin and running back Ja'Kobi Jackson. Both Ohio State starters have missed nearly a month of action as they are recovering from prolonged injuries. bmackay@dispatch.com @brimackay15 This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State adds another starting OL to availability report vs Northwestern

item.title: Dowling Catholic wins third straight IGHSAU swimming state title
item.description: IOWA CITY — The Dowling Catholic girls swimming and diving team might now have a dynasty. On Friday, Nov. 13, at the University of Iowa Campus Recreation and Wellness Center, coach Paul Eure and his Maroons team took first place with 294 points to win the program's third straight Iowa high school girls state swimming and diving title. This marks four state titles for the Maroons since 2019 and brings them closer to schools like Cedar Falls (9), Ames (8), and Bettendorf (7) for the most in the state. In addition to the 294 points, Dowling won two individual state titles, and the 400-yard freestyle relay team also took first place. "It just seems each year the group from the year before just gets a vision and they encourage the new swimmers to be part of that vision," Eure said. "There's no animosity towards each other about taking each other's spot. It's more about, 'hey let's do this together.'" The Maroons repeated as 400 freestyle relay champions with Qualley Charlotte, Taylor Hall, Gabby Freeseman, and Kimber Corwin. Charlotte and Corwin were the only two returns from last season's state title-winning relay team. Corwin added to her hardware by winning the 200-yard individual medley for the second-straight season. She also took home the 100-yard butterfly for the first time. "This was so exciting. We were a little unsure at the beginning, but as we kept getting closer to state, we started thinking about pink shirts more and more," Corwin said. "I'm so thankful for this team and all the girls." Dowling Catholic found success in a lot of events. Mylee Dirks took second in the diving event with 452 points. The 200-yard medley relay team placed third -- Charlotte took second in the 200-yard freestyle at 1:49.63 -- and Hall came in fifth in the 50-yard freestyle. Cedar Falls came in second with 209 points. And Bettendorf and Waukee Northwest shared the third-place trophy, each scoring 181 points. Bettendorf's quartet of Jaya Stacy, Emilia Surma, Brielle Andedo and Lillian Andedo had nice performances for the whole state to see. They came in first place in the 200-yard medley relay and broke the state record in the 200-yard freestyle relay. The previous time set back in 2018 was 1:33.50; the Bulldogs rewrote history at 1:33.14. Stacy took second in the 100-yard breaststroke, and together, the Andedo twins placed second in two events, and Lillian Andedo took first in the 50-yard freestyle. Ella Gardner from Cedar Falls won the 100-yard freestyle; Ames's Ellie McCorkle won the 500-yard freestyle, 200-yard freestyle and was named Athlete of the Year. Wahlert's Lucy Parson retained her title in the 100-yard breaststroke for the third straight season. item.description: CLEMSON, SC - NOVEMBER 13: Georgetown Hoyas center Vince Iwuchukwu (3) lays up a shot over Clemson Tigers forward David Fuchs (8) during a college basketball game between the Georgetown Hoyas and the Clemson Tigers on November 13, 2026, at Littlejohn Coliseum in Clemson, S.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It was a tale of two halves for the Clemson basketball team tonight. On the first chilly night of the fall, the Tigers’ first half matched the weather. After the teams traded buckets in the first seven minutes, Georgetown’s Jaland Low drilled a 3 to give the Hoyas a 17-14 lead with 13:42 left in the half. Clemson wouldn’t score again until a David Fuchs hook shot with 9:09 remaining made it 30-16. Not only did Clemson go ice cold on offense, but the defense also looked disinterested at best. Meanwhile, Georgetown was reliving John Thompson’s golden era, hitting every shot they launched at the rim. Basketball is a game of runs, and the Hoyas found themselves in the midst of an epic heater. When Clemson finally cleared their head and started playing basketball again, the score was 45-27 with 1:49 remaining in the half before Clemson hit a little run before halftime, giving the team the faintest whiff of momentum and making the score 47-32 heading into the break. The Tigers flipped the switch in the second half, thanks to Cole Certa and Ace Buckner’s scoring and a more consistent defensive and rebounding effort. With 13:18 remaining, the Tigers cut Georgetown’s 15-point halftime lead to 4 with a David Faulkner dunk, turning a game that looked like a lost cause in the first half into something worth watching. Unfortunately for Clemson, every time it looked like they were taking control, Georgetown’s veteran backcourt of Elmarko Jackson and Jaland Lowe had an answer. When Clemson took a 62-61 lead on a Cole Certa 3 with 8 minutes remaining, the Hoyas went down to the other end and matched it with a Jaland Lowe 3 to retake the lead. When a Cole Certa layup at the 6:23 mark put the Tigers up by 2, Elmarko Jackson responded with a mid-range jumper to tie it at 66-66 with 5:49 remaining.
